messages:
lina: ping — betapay's POC CI started failing overnight with 429s. they think it's our global quota even though the dashboard shows available credits. they hit it during a parallel end-to-end job run. any quick triage?

devon: can you grab a few failing request_ids and the route name? also how many concurrent jobs were they running?

lina: route=betapay-e2e, sample ids: r_8d7f, r_8d7g, r_8d7h. they ran 30 parallel runners with long chat prompts (avg ~280 tokens). logs show mixed 200 and 429s in bursts.

zarah: likely per-route throttling / token-window limit. our per-tenant counter is separate from per-route buckets. when many long requests hit the same route, the route window can saturate even if tenant quota has headroom.

lina: attaching small log excerpt: ```
[r_8d7f] route=betapay-e2e status=200 tokens=292
[r_8d7g] route=betapay-e2e status=429 reason=rate_limit hdr_retry_after=0
[r_8d7h] route=betapay-e2e status=429 reason=burst_window hdr_retry_after=0
```

devon: hdr_retry_after=0 is our quick-deny behavior for sliding refill schemes. we don't always calculate an exact next-available timestamp for short jittery bursts.

zarah: i checked quota logs — snippet: ```
[02:14:01] check route=betapay-e2e window=60s used=870 limit=750 -> deny burst_window
[02:14:02] adjust route=betapay-e2e +292 -> used=1162
[02:14:03] check tenant=betapay total_window=60s used=1162 limit=5000 -> allow
```

zarah: that shows route-level cap tripped but tenant-level still fine. it's consistent with concurrent long requests.

lina: customer asks why tokens_charged differs between requests — sometimes 0 on 429s, sometimes ~290 on 200s.

devon: 429s aren't charged; we only charge on success or partial streamed progress depending on model. long prompts spike tokens; also streaming responses can inflate in-flight accounting if not reconciled.

lina: betapay wants a short-term fix so their CI can pass this week — they'd prefer not to throttle down tests.

zarah: options: 1) advise them to add jitter/reduce concurrency to ~8-12 workers, 2) enable a temporary per-route demo-bump for 48h (ops change), or 3) have them use a reservation API to pre-allocate tokens for heavy jobs (we can enable preflight reservations for enterprise).

lina: can ops do a short demo bump? they have a live demo tomorrow.

ops-bot: finance check required for route bumps outside trial. current trial credit for betapay: $500 remaining.

finance: quick confirm — we can approve a 48h soft bump to route cap limited to +2x baseline for POC if sales signs off. will flag billing alert.

zarah: if we do bump, let's also add a small server-side advisory header on 429s that suggests scheduling/backoff, e.g., X-Redwood-Advice: "reduce concurrency or use reservation". it'll help their CI adapt.

devon: also propose a small client-side snippet for their test harness to handle 429s and avoid false negatives: ```
# pseudocode
while attempts < 4:
  resp = post('/v1/generate', body)
  if resp.status == 200: break
  if resp.status == 429:
    wait = min( (100 * 2**attempts) + jitter(), 2000 )  # ms
    sleep(wait/1000.0)
    attempts += 1
```

lina: i'll ask betapay to lower concurrency to 12 and add the backoff for now. please queue the ops bump as backup and confirm once finance ok.

zarah: follow-ups i'll own: 1) add advisory header and 2) raise SRE ticket to improve retry-after heuristics for sliding windows. devon: can you open a ticket for client docs?

devon: done — DOCS-3212 created with code snippets and guidance.

ops-bot: schedule: ops request queued (bump-request/betapay/48h) -> pending finance approval.

lina: thanks team — i'll update betapay and loop back after they run one adjusted CI. they also asked for a short writeup for their security team explaining data handling during POC; i'll open a separate thread for that.

finance: approved soft bump pending sales sign-off.

zarah: marking this thread for a quick postmortem after POC to capture any product tweaks we want to make for reservations and metrics visibility.
